examples.title: Series RLC step response
examples.description: 1 V DC switched onto R, L and C in series: an underdamped oscillation at 1.59 kHz. The smallest model, a good one to edit.

examples.title: RL load switched by a breaker
examples.description: A breaker closes at 5 ms and, after the opening command at 52 ms, interrupts at the next current zero. The Events tab lists both actions.

examples.title: Inverting amplifier with a dependent source
examples.description: An operational amplifier of gain 1e5 as a vcvs, with R_f / R_in = 10: the gain is -9.9989 at every instant, because the dependent source acts within the time step.

examples.title: Single line to ground fault behind a transformer
examples.description: A 66 kV source, a 50 km line and a YNd11 transformer, started from the steady state. Phase a is faulted at 0.1 s and cleared at a current zero. Has a frequency scan of the impedances seen from two buses.

examples.title: Energization of an open 100 km line
examples.description: Travelling waves on a distributed-parameter line: the open end reaches about 2.4 times the source peak. The frequency scan shows the resonances seen from the open end.

examples.title: Three areas joined by two travelling-wave lines
examples.description: Two sources feed a load bus over two lines; a three-phase fault on the load bus is cleared at the current zeros. The lines split the circuit into three parts that are solved separately.

examples.title: Synchronous machine: terminal fault and swing
examples.description: A 555 MVA generator against an infinite bus. A three-phase fault at its terminals lasts 70 ms; then the rotor swings at about 1.3 Hz.

examples.title: Islanded generator with excitation system and governor
examples.description: A load step of 10 % on a generator that runs alone: the frequency falls and settles 0.5 % low (droop), the excitation system restores the terminal voltage. 8 s in 80 000 steps.

examples.title: Transition through three times of a schedule
examples.description: A generator, a load and a grid followed through three hours of a schedule in one run: the set points ramp over 1 s and the run settles for 6 s, twice. The generator has an excitation system, a governor and a stabilizer; the load is switched in parts. Made by openkeito.pandapower.transition. 14.5 s in 145 000 steps.

examples.title: Grid-following converter: step of the active power
examples.description: The averaged model of a 2 MVA inverter with its phase-locked loop and current control. The active power reference steps from 1.0 to 1.6 MW at 0.1 s.

examples.title: Grid-following converter: current limit during a fault
examples.description: A fault takes the bus voltage to 0.5 per unit. The converter turns to reactive current and its current stays at the limit of 1.1 per unit; after the fault it returns to its operating point.

examples.title: Controlled current injection started in the steady state
examples.description: An averaged inverter written with control blocks (PLL, dq to abc) that reproduces the current of the phasor solution from t = 0: the run stays in its steady state.

examples.title: WECC generic IBR (REGCA1 / REECA1 / REPCA1)
examples.description: A 10 MVA inverter-based resource built with WECC generic plant, electrical, and converter controls using piecewise-linear limits (VDL1, VDL2, LVPL, LVACM) and dynamic PI/lag limits. A three-phase fault at 0.2 s dips the voltage and triggers reactive current support and active current limiting before recovering.

examples.title: Buck converter, open loop
examples.description: 100 V, 10 kHz PWM with duty 0.41: the output settles at 41 V. 20 000 steps of 1 µs with about 800 switching events.

examples.title: Buck converter, switching instants within the step
examples.description: The same converter with a ten times larger step and "switching": "interpolated": the switch and the diode act between grid points (see the times in the Events tab).

examples.title: Buck converter, PI voltage control
examples.description: A PI controller on the duty holds the output at 30 V. 100 000 steps, one row in ten recorded.

examples.title: Diode bridge with capacitor input
examples.description: A single-phase bridge charging a capacitor: short current pulses near the voltage peaks. 100 000 rows, to try the chart on a long result.

examples.title: Ideal transformer of a vcvs and a cccs
examples.description: A vcvs and a cccs make an ideal transformer of ratio 10, which feeds a diode bridge with a capacitor; the switching instants lie within the time steps.

examples.title: Six-pulse thyristor rectifier
examples.description: Six thyristors fired at 30 deg after the natural commutation, with 1 mH per phase: the DC current rises to 50 A and the average DC voltage is the textbook 452.8 V. The firing and the end of each commutation lie between grid points (see the Events tab).

examples.title: Inrush current of a saturable transformer
examples.description: A transformer with an open secondary switched on at a voltage zero: the core saturates and the first current peak is 1.85 times the rated peak.

examples.title: Half-wave rectifier with a saturable reactor
examples.description: A reactor with a three-segment flux–current curve in series with a diode; the current peaks in the saturated segment.

examples.title: Surge arrester limiting a current surge
examples.description: A 20 kA surge into a 400 Ω line protected by a metal-oxide arrester: 171 kV instead of 8 MV.

examples.title: Current control with a controlled voltage source
examples.description: A PI controller whose zero cancels the pole of an RL circuit: the current follows a step of its reference like a first-order lag.

examples.title: Phase-locked loop
examples.description: A PLL locks on a 50.5 Hz voltage, once as one block and once built from elementary blocks; both give the same frequency.

examples.title: A tour of the control blocks
examples.description: One set point shaped by a rate limiter, lags, a lead-lag, a delay, a limiter and more. Choose the signals to compare.

examples.title: Expression control blocks
examples.description: Single-input, multi-input, and variables-mapped mathematical expressions (model format 0.8) driving a controlled current source into an RC load.

examples.title: Gate from comparison and logical operators
examples.description: The gate (x > 0.3) && (x < 0.8) of an expression (model format 0.10) closes a 100 V chopper while a sine wave lies between 0.3 and 0.8. The switch acts where the sine wave crosses the band, between grid points (see the Events tab).
